name: Magnolia Sanctum
reason: Source 'Yulan Holy Land' was localized as 'Magnolia Sanctum': 'yulan' is Chinese for magnolia, and 'Sanctum' replaces 'Holy Land' to fit the Western fantasy register.
description: A human Holy Land active during the Samsara Abyss arc (Eps 1136-1155). Its Saint Lord shields Abner from an attack, and one of its cultivators claims a powered-down automaton to take back to the Sanctum for study.

name: Cassian
reason: The source character's single-syllable name 'Mie' was fully localized to 'Cassian', a Western name fitting his role as a devoted royal guard; the episode line 'Cassian loves his queen' mirrors the source line 'Mie likes my Queen.'
description: A spear-wielding warrior devoted to Queen Lavender, serving alongside Maren, Taryn, and Paige. He nearly died protecting her while exploring The Endless Abyss, and his eyes soften whenever he sees her; the group relentlessly pursues Zane on the queen's orders.

name: Gilded Warden
reason: The source's 30,000-foot golden Buddha guarding the ancient temple was renamed the 'Gilded Warden' to strip the Buddhist religious reference while keeping the image of a colossal golden guardian.
description: A giant, sentient golden guardian dwelling deep in a temple sanctuary within the Illusion Battlefield (Eps 1219-1223). Perfectly aware of Chaos Energy, it commands the temple's stone guardians, yet ultimately chooses to let Zane go, its composure wavering when it feels his gaze.

name: Five-Element Finger Chain
reason: Source term 'Five Element Finger Chain' was carried over nearly verbatim, hyphenated for English readability.
description: A hand-worn armament used by a female opponent in the Illusion Battlefield arc (Eps 1233-1239). When it glows, it channels its wielder's accumulated energy into Five-Element Palm Print attacks.

name: Five-Element Palm Print
reason: A technique name rendered in the same pattern as the source's Five Element Finger Chain, from which it is produced; the exact source phrase was not found in the evidence.
description: An offensive technique generated through the Five-Element Finger Chain: the wielder's energy transforms into a palm print radiating killing intent, fired at Zane in Ep 1238.

name: Five-Element
reason: The classical Chinese 'Five Elements' concept from the source was kept as the hyphenated modifier 'Five-Element' for powers and techniques.
description: The five-element power system underlying techniques in the late Illusion Battlefield arc, including House Kincaid's Five-Element fusion technique and the Five-Element power expended by the Finger Chain's wielder.

name: Cain
reason: The character's Chinese name 'Li Chengyan' was fully localized to 'Cain', a short Western name; his death scene (hooked and dragged into the darkness) matches the source chapter exactly.
description: A human warrior in the Illusion Battlefield's darkness region (Eps 1274-1276). He is snared by a hook, yanked into the suffocating darkness before he can finish his scream, and killed, bursting into Illusion Points and being sent back to the main city.

name: Priscilla
reason: The source figure is known only by the title 'Ninth Palace Master'; the adaptation gave her the personal name 'Priscilla', an elegant Western name befitting a senior power.
description: A senior powerhouse appearing at the very end of the show (Eps 1319-1320) who, before a watching room, personally leads the newly ascended Tia away, mirroring the source's Ninth Palace Master taking a just-ascended woman under her wing.

name: Mervin Thorne
reason: The character's Chinese name 'Sima Yulong' was fully localized to a Western name; 'Mervin' with the surname 'Thorne' marks him as a proud local genius of the Myriad Spirit House arc.
description: A furious local genius in the Myriad Spirit House arc (Eps 1031-1037), corresponding to Sima Yulong, the top-ranked prodigy of the source's Spiritual Martial Saint Land. He and his group rage that an ascender from an unknown Lower World was chosen over all of them, before finally understanding the truth.

name: Mason
reason: The character's Chinese name 'Jiang Yunfei' was fully localized to 'Mason', a blunt, rugged US name fitting a brutish sect enforcer; his cackling attack with razor-sharp energy on his hands matches Jiang Yunfei of the Blood Wood Cliff.
description: A Bloodwood Cliff warrior at Peak Soul Realm who tries to seize Zane at the Dragon Soar Arena (Eps 451-452), known for stopping at nothing once set on a goal. Zane takes him down effortlessly with a single punch, stunning the onlookers.

name: Men of Basalt
reason: The source's 'Black Tortoises' (Xuanwu, the creature basalt is named after in Chinese) attacking in the Outer Trial were localized as the 'Men of Basalt', keeping the stone-hard defensive image.
description: Heavily armored attackers forming a wave of the Outer Trial gauntlet (Eps 468-469), renowned for incredible defensive strength. Zane confidently leaves them to his sword spirit Lily while he goes to steal points from other competitors.

name: Pathforged Realm
reason: The source's dao-platform body-refining stage was renamed the 'Pathforged Realm' to convey forging one's own path in a Western fantasy register.
description: A major body-refining stage (Eps 489-600) said to be harder to achieve than Inner-Core or Spirit-Tribulation. Establishing it requires first forging the Confluence Platform within oneself, and it comprises eight platforms, each corresponding to a move of the Stellar Body taught by the Red Dragon.

name: Cloud-Chaser Lion
reason: Source term 'Cloud Chasing Lion' was lightly reworded to 'Cloud-Chaser Lion' for smoother English phrasing.
description: A Legendary Beast famed for insane speed, capable of compressing space when running flat out. Zane forges his Confluence Platform from a Cloud-Chaser Lion's jade bone, letting him tap the beast's speed talent directly.

name: Confluence Platform
reason: The source's 'dao platform' was renamed 'Confluence Platform' to remove the untranslatable 'dao' while conveying a convergence point of the body's energies.
description: The foundational platform a body refiner forges within himself to establish the Pathforged Realm (Eps 562-661). Zane's is made from a Cloud-Chaser Lion's bone, granting him the beast's speed and unlocking the first move of the Stellar Body, Star Shakes the Earth; establishing it skyrockets his physical limits.

name: Elder Kingsley
reason: The source's human leader 'Lord Jing' in the Tower of Sin was localized to 'Elder Kingsley', a stately Western name echoing 'Jing' phonetically and suiting a human War Lord.
description: The human War Lord inside the Tower of Sin (Eps 579-623), who summons Zane through Olivia and forms a mutual-aid alliance with him ('We help each other'). He is repeatedly impressed by Zane's composure and revises his expectations of the young warrior upward after meeting him.

name: Colin and Neil
issues: Compound phrase bundling two distinct characters, Colin and Neil, the two Ogre War Sages; not a single entity. Mentions belong to the individual characters.
reason: Dropped as a conjunction of two character names rather than an entity in its own right.

name: Colin
reason: An Ogre War Sage of the Tower of Sin arc given the Western name 'Colin'; no specific source counterpart could be identified in the evidence.
description: One of two Ogre War Sages, alongside Neil, in the Tower of Sin arc (Eps 612-613). The pair shoot toward the Tower of Sin's doors like living cannonballs at incredible speed.

name: House Shaw
reason: The source's 'Zhuo Family' of Cloud Sea City was localized as 'House Shaw', following the adaptation's Legacy House naming convention.
description: A Legacy House active around Eps 711-723, fielding warriors as strong as the Spirit-Tribulation Realm. One of its masters is left ashen-faced in battle, and its head appears in Ep 722, gravely shaking his head at the situation.

name: Heavenly Stellar Secret Realm
reason: Source term 'Heavenly Star Secret Realm' was lightly reworded to 'Heavenly Stellar Secret Realm' for the adaptation.
description: The most dangerous of the Sacred Feather Sea's hidden realms (Eps 792-796), far deadlier than the Feather Emperor's and Divine Emperor's Secret Realms. One of the three secret lands opens each year, and Zane knows he cannot simply charge into this one.

name: Violet Ascendancy Sect
reason: The source's 'Ten Thousand Purple Jade Tower' (also 'Myriad Purple Jade Tower'), whose cultivation demands a pure heart, few desires, and severed mortal bonds, was renamed the 'Violet Ascendancy Sect', keeping the purple motif in a Western sect name.
description: A nunnery-like sect led by Krista Donovan (Eps 966-968), whose members, like the purple-robed Bridget, must have few worldly desires and sever all ties to their past lives. Its millions of flying swords can fill the sky in a roaring cascade of steel.

name: Master Andrew
reason: The character's Chinese name 'Luo Chengyun' (Young Master Chengyun, Luo Junyi's eldest son) was fully localized to 'Andrew', with the 'Master' honorific preserved to mark his young-master status in the family.
description: Zane's arrogant cousin and the Lowell family's reigning young master in the earliest episodes (Eps 7-14). Petitioners plead to him with fake tears for help, and he sneers at 'Cousin Zane' before their confrontation in the Family Training Day deathmatches.

name: Family Training Day
reason: The source family's deathmatch gathering was localized as 'Family Training Day', a milder-sounding event name for the Western adaptation; the exact source term was not found in the evidence.
description: A huge Lowell family event held early in the show (Eps 10-30), featuring sanctioned duels including the Fatal Duel. Zane pins all his hopes on winning there to claim his freedom, while his enemies plot their revenge for the same day.

name: Demon General
reason: Source term 'Demon General' was retained verbatim as the rank name for high-tier demons.
description: A high-tier demon rank and the first significant threat Zane faces, during the demon-fighting trial arc (Eps 113-116). A Demon General has bark-thick hands and such power that even a flawlessly coordinated three-man team only barely matches one; Zane charging one as a mere high-level candidate stuns onlookers.

name: Concussive Blast
reason: One of House Solomon's (source: Family Zhu's) infamous Hidden Weapons; the specific source weapon name was not identifiable from the evidence.
description: An infamous Hidden Weapon of House Solomon, housed in an Ornate Box (Eps 117-128). It is powerful enough that being targeted by one is described as nearly being vaporized.

name: Bone Spurs
reason: A demon attack rendered descriptively as 'Bone Spurs' for the Western adaptation; no specific source term was found in the evidence.
description: A barrage attack unleashed from the bodies of Demon Commanders during the demon trial arc (Eps 120-123).

name: Underworld
reason: The setting's hell/afterworld, localizing the source's hell and netherworld references into a single consistent term used in oaths, threats, and lore.
description: The hell-like afterworld of the setting, invoked across the show (Eps 123-1314): forbidden Hellfire is known only to the Underworld's most formidable demons, enemies snarl at victims to 'journey to the Underworld', and it also appears in idioms like 'What in the Underworld'.

name: Shadow Dragon
reason: In Ep 128 Zane's Nether Essence corrupts the Imperial commander's Five-Clawed Golden Dragon (a source entity) into a darkened dragon he names the 'Shadow Dragon'; the name itself is an adaptation coinage for the corrupted form.
description: A massive energy dragon, originally the Imperial Army commander's golden dragon, whose radiant scales darken to blackish-purple when Zane's Nether Essence corrupts it from within (Eps 128-129). It submits to Zane as its new master, though it cannot break through a barrier no matter how it claws and bites.

name: Menacing Aura
reason: A hostile energy from the source's cage-trap sequence rendered descriptively as 'Menacing Aura'; the exact source term was not found in the evidence.
description: A hostile, heat-like energy within a cage-trap (Ep 145) that seeps into consciousness and probes at the soul. It rushes toward any breach like water seeking its level, desperately maintaining the cage's integrity, which Zane exploits.

name: Magic Circle
reason: The source's array/formation concept was localized as 'Magic Circle'; the master sheet confirms this is canonical and explicitly NOT 'Runic Array'.
description: Protective formation magic used in sect trials and grounds (Eps 41-147). Layered circles ring important areas, and within a trial's Magic Circle actual death is prevented even though the pain remains one hundred percent real.

name: Stryker
reason: The character's Chinese name 'Bai Sha' was fully localized to 'Roman Stryker', an aggressive Western name fitting a professional killer; his death to the thrown Shattered Dagger matches Bai Sha's death to the broken flying knife in the source.
description: One half of the Diabolic Duo, a pair of halberd-wielding assassins who ambush Zane at Dragon's Keep alongside his partner Graves (Eps 75-77, per the master sheet an antagonist across Eps 65-83). Confident his legendary halberd could parry anything, he is beheaded when Zane's Shattered Dagger slices the weapon clean in two.

name: Abyssal Pikes
reason: Monstrous fish from the source's trial sequence localized as 'Abyssal Pikes'; the exact source creature name was not found in the evidence.
description: Massive red pike-like creatures with sharp golden scales that erupt from the water during a trial gauntlet (Eps 152-153). Zane dodges them to land unharmed on the central spire.

name: Tyson
reason: A Blackwood House retainer given the strong Western name 'Tyson' fitting a bodyguard; no specific source counterpart was identifiable from the evidence.
description: A Blackwood House bodyguard (Eps 205-207) who pledged unwavering loyalty to his young master after being granted a second life, shadowing him with total devotion. He exemplifies the house's talent for finding and cultivating diamonds in the rough.

name: Level Two
reason: Dropped as a generic level qualifier ('Level Two of the Adept Realm'), a fragment of realm-stage phrasing rather than a standalone entity.

name: Warren
reason: The source's 'Mentor Wen', who leads disciples through the Peak Competition, was localized to 'Master Warren', a Western name echoing 'Wen' phonetically.
description: A Misty Peak master overseeing competition logistics (Eps 238-241, per the master sheet from Ep 235). Stern in defending his students' standing, his eyes shoot wide with shock when Zane offers him a remarkable pill.

name: Meteor Flame
reason: A flame technique from the competition arc localized as 'Meteor Flame'; the exact source term was not found in the evidence.
description: A rare and very real flame wielded by Mack in the competition arc (Ep 245), dangerous even amid illusory stone men. Mack cannot summon it at will.

name: Top-Grade Spirit Weapon
reason: The highest grade within the canonical Tier-2 'Spirit Weapon' class, following the source's weapon-grade terminology for the Western adaptation.
description: The highest grade of Spirit Weapon (Tier 2), so rare that many warriors never see one in their lives (Eps 250-561). Zane meticulously refines his own body to the durability of a Top-Grade Spirit Weapon, leaving him with virtually no weaknesses, though the grade still sits well below Sacred Weapons.

name: Elder
reason: Dropped as a generic honorific/title: the mentions span many different individuals (an Elder of the Skyreach Sect, Elder Ingrid, Elder Boris, Elders and Guardians generally) rather than one entity.
